name: Kedgeree
description: The British breakfast that never quite forgot it was Indian — smoked haddock and basmati rice perfumed with curry leaf and cardamom, topped with soft-boiled eggs and parsley, a colonial collision that became its own distinct thing.

name: Key Lime Curd
description: A pale, sun-yellow curd with the floral, nearly tropical tartness of true key limes — thickened slowly over a double boiler until it coats a spoon like liquid satin.

ingredients.note: Fresh key lime juice (about 12–15 key limes)

name: Florida Key Lime Pie
description: A trembling, pale-yellow custard made from the tiny, intensely perfumed key limes of the Florida Keys — bracingly tart and sweetened only by sweetened condensed milk, set in a buttery graham cracker crust that shatters at the first fork.

ingredients.note: Fresh key lime juice (about 20–25 key limes)
Heavy cream, chilled, for whipped topping

name: Florida Key Lime Pie (gluten-free)
description: A trembling, pale-yellow custard made from the tiny, intensely perfumed key limes of the Florida Keys — bracingly tart and sweetened only by sweetened condensed milk, set in a buttery gluten-free graham cracker crust that shatters at the first fork. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free biscuits instead of digestive biscuits.

ingredients.note: instead of Graham cracker crumbs (about 11 full crackers)
Fresh key lime juice (about 20–25 key limes)
Heavy cream, chilled, for whipped topping

name: Rice Kheer
description: India's ancient milk-rice pudding — short-grain rice simmered slowly in whole milk until it thickens to a creamy porridge, perfumed with cardamom and saffron, finished with toasted pistachios and rose water.

ingredients.note: Short-grain white rice (gobindobhog or arborio), rinsed
Green cardamom pods, seeds only, freshly ground
Dried rose petals or edible silver leaf (vark)

name: Rice Kheer (nut-free)
description: India's ancient milk-rice pudding — short-grain rice simmered slowly in whole milk until it thickens to a creamy porridge, perfumed with cardamom and saffron, finished with pumpkin seeds and rose water. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of pistachios.

ingredients.note: Short-grain white rice (gobindobhog or arborio), rinsed
Green cardamom pods, seeds only, freshly ground
Dried rose petals or edible silver leaf (vark)

name: Khichdi
description: Rice and yellow moong dal cooked down together to a soft, porridge-like whole, tempered with a sizzling spoonful of ghee, cumin, and turmeric — the great Indian comfort food, restorative and deeply nourishing, equally at home on a sick day or a festival table.

ingredients.note: Yellow moong dal, split and hulled

name: Khichdi (gluten-free)
description: Rice and yellow moong dal cooked down together to a soft, porridge-like whole, tempered with a sizzling spoonful of ghee, cumin, and turmeric — the great Indian comfort food, restorative and deeply nourishing, equally at home on a sick day or a festival table. This gluten-free version uses asafoetida (gluten-free) instead of asafoetida.

ingredients.note: Yellow moong dal, split and hulled

name: Kitchari
description: The Ayurvedic healing porridge of India — split mung dal and basmati rice cooked together with golden ghee, cumin, and turmeric until they dissolve into a warmly fragrant, deeply nourishing, easily digestible whole that is more than the sum of its parts.

name: Kladdkaka
description: A Swedish fudge cake deliberately baked underdone — the edges set into a thin, crackled crust while the center remains dense, gooey, and almost raw-textured, eaten cold from the fridge with a dusting of icing sugar and a cloud of whipped cream.

name: Kladdkaka (gluten-free)
description: A Swedish fudge cake deliberately baked underdone — the edges set into a thin, crackled crust while the center remains dense, gooey, and almost raw-textured, eaten cold from the fridge with a dusting of icing sugar and a cloud of whipped cream. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Kofta
description: Hand-formed lamb and onion cylinders threaded on flat skewers, heavy with allspice and raw parsley — grilled over charcoal until the outside is dark and crackling while the inside stays pink-tinged and impossibly juicy.

ingredients.note: Brown onion, grated on large holes
Aleppo pepper flakes or red chilli flakes

name: Korean Bulgogi
description: Thin ribbons of beef, lacquered in a pear-soy marinade, hit a screaming hot grill and caramelize in seconds — sweet, smoky, and impossibly tender with every char-edged bite.

ingredients.note: Beef ribeye or sirloin, sliced 3mm thin

name: Korean Bulgogi (gluten-free)
description: Thin ribbons of beef, lacquered in a pear-soy marinade, hit a screaming hot grill and caramelize in seconds — sweet, smoky, and impossibly tender with every char-edged bite. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef ribeye or sirloin, sliced 3mm thin

name: Korean Fried Chicken
description: The double-fry is not a technique — it is a philosophy. First fry sets the crust and begins rendering the fat; second fry shatters the crust into something approaching glass, a shell so thin and crisp it crackles audibly across a room. The yangnyeom sauce — a lacquer of gochujang, honey, and garlic — clings without softening it, and the whole thing glows under kitchen light like lacquerware.

ingredients.note: Chicken wings or drumettes (or bone-in pieces)
Neutral oil for deep frying (canola or rice bran); for frying (only some is absorbed)
Garlic cloves, minced to a paste
Toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions

name: Korean Fried Chicken (gluten-free)
description: The double-fry is not a technique — it is a philosophy. First fry sets the crust and begins rendering the fat; second fry shatters the crust into something approaching glass, a shell so thin and crisp it crackles audibly across a room. The yangnyeom sauce — a lacquer of gochujang, honey, and garlic — clings without softening it, and the whole thing glows under kitchen light like lacquerware. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free gochujang instead of gochujang, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Chicken wings or drumettes (or bone-in pieces)
Neutral oil for deep frying (canola or rice bran); for frying (only some is absorbed)
Garlic cloves, minced to a paste
Toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions

name: Korean Galbi-Jjim (Braised Beef Short Ribs)
description: Soy-sweet short ribs slow-braised with Asian pear, garlic, and ginger until the collagen melts into a glossy, lacquered sauce that clings to bone-loosened beef.

ingredients.note: Bone-in beef short ribs (flanken-cut or English-cut)
Water or beef stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water
Toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallion
Gochujang or dried chili flakes (optional heat)

name: Korean Galbi-Jjim (Braised Beef Short Ribs) (gluten-free)
description: Soy-sweet short ribs slow-braised with Asian pear, garlic, and ginger until the collagen melts into a glossy, lacquered sauce that clings to bone-loosened beef. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Bone-in beef short ribs (flanken-cut or English-cut)
Water or beef stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water
Toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallion

name: Korean Haemul Pajeon
description: A wide, golden seafood and green onion pancake with a shatteringly crisp exterior and a tender, eggy interior — the kind of thing every Korean home makes when the first rain of the season falls.

ingredients.note: Green onions (scallions), trimmed to pan length
Raw shrimp, peeled and roughly chopped

name: Korean Haemul Pajeon (gluten-free)
description: A wide, golden seafood and green onion pancake with a shatteringly crisp exterior and a tender, eggy interior — the kind of thing every Korean home makes when the first rain of the season falls. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Green onions (scallions), trimmed to pan length
Raw shrimp, peeled and roughly chopped

name: Korean Pajeon (Scallion Pancake)
description: A wide, flat pancake of rice flour batter loaded with bundles of whole scallions, fried in a generous pool of oil until the underside is a shatteringly crisp lacework of golden crust and the interior is chewy, savoury, and yielding.

ingredients.note: Scallions (green onions), whole or halved lengthwise

name: Korean Pajeon (Scallion Pancake) (gluten-free)
description: A wide, flat pancake of rice flour batter loaded with bundles of whole scallions, fried in a generous pool of oil until the underside is a shatteringly crisp lacework of golden crust and the interior is chewy, savoury, and yielding. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Scallions (green onions), whole or halved lengthwise

name: Galbi (Korean Short Ribs)
description: Flanken-cut beef short ribs marinated in a caramelizing blend of Asian pear, soy, sesame, garlic, and ginger — the fruit enzymes tenderizing the meat while the sugars char to a bittersweet crust over roaring charcoal.

ingredients.note: Beef short ribs, flanken-cut (1 cm thick across bones)
Asian pear, grated (or kiwi, half piece)

name: Galbi (Korean Short Ribs) (gluten-free)
description: Flanken-cut beef short ribs marinated in a caramelizing blend of Asian pear, soy, sesame, garlic, and ginger — the fruit enzymes tenderizing the meat while the sugars char to a bittersweet crust over roaring charcoal. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef short ribs, flanken-cut (1 cm thick across bones)
Asian pear, grated (or kiwi, half piece)

name: Sigeumchi Namul (Korean Sesame Spinach)
description: Blanched spinach squeezed to silk and dressed in toasted sesame, garlic, and soy — the simplest banchan in the Korean table, and the one that disappears first from the bowl.

name: Sigeumchi Namul (Korean Sesame Spinach) (gluten-free)
description: Blanched spinach squeezed to silk and dressed in toasted sesame, garlic, and soy — the simplest banchan in the Korean table, and the one that disappears first from the bowl. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

name: Kuku Sabzi
description: The Persian herb frittata of Nowruz — more herb than egg, so dense with dill, parsley, coriander, and fenugreek that it slices dark green, with walnut halves and tart dried barberries studding each piece like garnets in jade.

ingredients.note: Fresh or dried fenugreek leaves (methi), finely chopped

name: Kuku Sabzi (nut-free)
description: The Persian herb frittata of Nowruz — more herb than egg, so dense with dill, parsley, coriander, and fenugreek that it slices dark green, with pumpkin seeds halves and tart dried barberries studding each piece like garnets in jade. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

ingredients.note: Fresh or dried fenugreek leaves (methi), finely chopped
instead of Walnut halves, roughly broken

name: Kulfi
description: The ancient frozen dessert of the Subcontinent — whole milk reduced low and slow to a thick, fudgy paste, then sweetened with condensed milk and shot through with cardamom, saffron, and crushed pistachios before being set in conical molds.

name: Kulfi (nut-free)
description: The ancient frozen dessert of the Subcontinent — whole milk reduced low and slow to a thick, fudgy paste, then sweetened with condensed milk and shot through with cardamom, saffron, and crushed pumpkin seeds before being set in conical molds. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of pistachios.

name: Kung Pao Chicken (Gong Bao Ji Ding)
description: Cubed chicken thigh, quick-velveted in cornstarch, meets a fiercely hot wok alongside dried Sichuan chilies and fried peanuts in a sauce that balances the four elements of Sichuan cuisine — numbing, hot, sour, and sweet — in a single chopstick load. The chilies go in whole and stay whole: their job is to perfume the oil, not disintegrate into the dish.

ingredients.note: Dried Sichuan red chilies (whole, stems on)
Cornstarch mixed with cold water (1:2, for sauce)

name: Kung Pao Chicken (Gong Bao Ji Ding) (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Cubed chicken thigh, quick-velveted in cornstarch, meets a fiercely hot wok alongside dried Sichuan chilies and fried toasted sunflower seeds in a sauce that balances the four elements of Sichuan cuisine — numbing, hot, sour, and sweet — in a single chopstick load. The chilies go in whole and stay whole: their job is to perfume the oil, not disintegrate into the dish. This gluten- & nut-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine, sunflower seeds instead of peanuts, rice vinegar instead of chinese black vinegar.

ingredients.note: instead of Light soy sauce (for marinade)
Dried Sichuan red chilies (whole, stems on)
instead of Light soy sauce (for sauce)
Cornstarch mixed with cold water (1:2, for sauce)

name: Lamb Kofta
description: Hand-blended ground lamb mixed with onion, parsley, and warm spices, molded onto flat skewers and grilled over charcoal until charred outside and juicy within.

ingredients.note: Ground lamb (20–25% fat, not too lean)
Yellow onion (grated on a box grater)
Cayenne pepper or Aleppo chili flakes
Lamb fat or neutral oil (if meat is very lean)

name: Lamb Rogan Josh
description: The crown jewel of Kashmiri wazwan cooking — bone-in lamb slow-braised in a brick-red gravy built from Kashmiri chilis, yogurt, and a regiment of whole spices, arriving at the table deeply fragrant and moderately spiced, with a silky, enveloping sauce that coats the meat in shades of rust and crimson.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder or neck (bone-in, cut into 5cm pieces)
Dried Kashmiri chilis (whole, stemmed and seeded)
Kashmiri chili powder (for the gravy base)
Green cardamom pods (hari elaichi, lightly cracked)
Warm water or light stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Lamb Rogan Josh (gluten-free)
description: The crown jewel of Kashmiri wazwan cooking — bone-in lamb slow-braised in a brick-red gravy built from Kashmiri chilis, yogurt, and a regiment of whole spices, arriving at the table deeply fragrant and moderately spiced, with a silky, enveloping sauce that coats the meat in shades of rust and crimson. This gluten-free version uses asafoetida (gluten-free) instead of asafoetida.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder or neck (bone-in, cut into 5cm pieces)
Dried Kashmiri chilis (whole, stemmed and seeded)
Kashmiri chili powder (for the gravy base)
Green cardamom pods (hari elaichi, lightly cracked)
Warm water or light stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Lamb Shawarma
description: Lamb shoulder marinated in a warm-spiced yogurt paste — turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, coriander, and cardamom — then slow-roasted until the outside caramelizes into dark, spiced bark while the inside stays tender enough to shred with a fork.

name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
description: Bone-in lamb shoulder braised for two hours in a perfumed cloud of ras el hanout, saffron, and ginger until it falls apart in the hand — then finished with the sharp salinity of preserved lemon and the brine of cracked green olives.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5cm pieces
Preserved lemon rind, pith removed, finely sliced

name: Larb Moo
description: A Northeastern Thai salad of minced pork cooked in its own rendered fat and doused with lime juice and fish sauce, the meat still steaming when it hits a blizzard of fresh herbs, shallots, and toasted rice powder that soaks up every last drop of the hot, sour, savoury dressing.

ingredients.note: Khao khua: raw glutinous or jasmine rice, dry-toasted
Asian shallots (4–5 small), thinly sliced into rings
Lemongrass stalk, inner tender part only, very finely sliced
Cabbage wedges and cucumber slices, to serve

name: British Lemon Curd
description: Egg yolks, butter, and fierce citrus cook into a molten, traffic-light-yellow cream that strikes the tongue with a bright, almost painful tartness before butter smooths it into silk. Spread thick on warm scones or spooned over meringue, it is concentrated sunshine in a jar.

ingredients.note: Lemon zest, finely grated (from same lemons)

name: Lemon-Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs
description: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs roasted at high heat until the skin shatters like lacquered glass and the fat underneath has rendered completely into the meat. The lemon zest and herb paste rubbed under the skin blooms and perfumes the fat as it renders, so every bite tastes of thyme and citrus from the inside out.

ingredients.note: Lemon zest (from 1 lemon) + juice (half the lemon)
Garlic cloves, minced to a paste

name: Lemon Posset
description: Heavy cream and sugar boiled together and set with nothing but fresh lemon juice — a two-ingredient miracle that turns the acid into a natural gelling agent, producing a wobbling, intensely lemony cream.

name: Lentil Sloppy Joes
description: Brown lentils simmered in a thick, tangy-sweet tomato sauce with peppers, onion, and smoked paprika, spooned generously onto buttery toasted buns. Messy, saucy, and deeply savory.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock; made up to 700 ml with boiling water

name: Red Lentil Soup
description: Turkey's most democratic dish — red lentils dissolved to velvet, bloomed with paprika-butter at the table, and finished with a jolt of lemon that transforms humble into electric.

ingredients.note: Vegetable or chicken stock; made up to 800 ml with boiling water

name: Libum
description: Cato's sacrificial cake, reborn for the table — fresh ricotta beaten to a curd-flecked batter, bound with egg and a little spelt flour, mounded onto bay leaves and baked beneath a covered pot until the edges crack golden. Split warm and drowned in dark honey, it eats like the oldest cheesecake in the world.

name: Lion's Head Meatballs (Shi Zi Tou)
description: Enormous pork meatballs — each one nearly the size of a fist — braise slowly in their own rendered fat and a dark, amber Shaoxing wine broth until the outer crust gives way to an interior so tender and yielding it trembles when the chopstick touches it, the napa cabbage around them having dissolved into silky ribbons that carry the concentrated braising juice. The name honors the meatball's resemblance to a lion's head surrounded by its cabbage mane.

ingredients.note: Ground pork (30% fat — do not use lean)
Napa cabbage, outer leaves separated whole
Light chicken or pork stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Lion's Head Meatballs (Shi Zi Tou) (gluten-free)
description: Enormous pork meatballs — each one nearly the size of a fist — braise slowly in their own rendered fat and a dark, amber Shaoxing wine broth until the outer crust gives way to an interior so tender and yielding it trembles when the chopstick touches it, the napa cabbage around them having dissolved into silky ribbons that carry the concentrated braising juice. The name honors the meatball's resemblance to a lion's head surrounded by its cabbage mane. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of dark soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine.

ingredients.note: Ground pork (30% fat — do not use lean)
Napa cabbage, outer leaves separated whole
Light chicken or pork stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Lobster Bisque
description: The grandest of French bisques — whole lobsters roasted and deglazed with cognac, simmered in white wine and fish stock with tomatoes and tarragon, strained twice and mounted with cream into a pale coral soup of extraordinary richness.

name: Lobster Thermidor
description: The grand-dame of belle-époque cookery — sweet poached lobster folded back into a mustard-and-cognac cream sauce, heaped into its own scarlet shell, blanketed with Gruyère and run under the grill until the top blisters gold and the whole thing arrives bubbling, fragrant with tarragon and flamed brandy.

ingredients.note: Live lobster (about 600 g each, or cooked tail & claw meat)

name: Loukoumades
description: Greece's ancient honey-dipped fritters — yeasted dough dropped by the spoonful into hot oil where they puff into irregular golden spheres, pulled and immediately drenched in warm honey and dusted with cinnamon and crushed walnut.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for frying (sunflower or rice bran); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Ma Po Tofu
description: Silken tofu trembling in a Sichuan doubanjiang sauce with ground pork and a numbing, tingly cloud of freshly ground Sichuan peppercorn — one of the world's great flavor experiences, a dish where the 'ma' (numbing) and 'la' (spicy) arrive as two separate sensations.

ingredients.note: Silken or soft tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
Chicken or pork stock; made up to 300 ml with boiling water
Dried red chili flakes (er jing tiao or facing heaven chili)
Cornstarch mixed with 60 g cold water (slurry)

name: Maafe (West African Peanut Stew)
description: A Malian and Senegalese stew where peanut butter melts into a tomato and broth base, enveloping braised lamb and sweet potato in a sauce so rich and unctuous it clings to the spoon like liquid velvet — every bowl a tightrope between nutty sweetness and savory, peppery depth.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm pieces
Canned whole tomatoes, crushed by hand
Chicken or lamb stock; made up to 250 ml with boiling water

name: Maafe (West African Sunflower seed Stew) (nut-free)
description: A Malian and Senegalese stew where sunflower seed butter melts into a tomato and broth base, enveloping braised lamb and sweet potato in a sauce so rich and unctuous it clings to the spoon like liquid velvet — every bowl a tightrope between nutty sweetness and savory, peppery depth. This nut-free version uses sunflower seed butter instead of peanut butter.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm pieces
Canned whole tomatoes, crushed by hand
Chicken or lamb stock; made up to 250 ml with boiling water

name: Baked Mac and Cheese
description: Macaroni suspended in a molten, sharp cheddar béchamel, crowned with a golden breadcrumb crust that shatters into the cream below — the kind of mac and cheese that renders all the boxed versions a distant memory.

ingredients.note: Sharp cheddar, freshly grated (plus Gruyère optional)
Kosher salt, dry mustard, white pepper, nutmeg
Panko breadcrumbs toasted in butter (for topping)

name: Baked Mac and Cheese (gluten-free)
description: Macaroni suspended in a molten, sharp cheddar béchamel, crowned with a golden breadcrumb crust that shatters into the cream below — the kind of mac and cheese that renders all the boxed versions a distant memory. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta, gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs.

ingredients.note: instead of Elbow macaroni or cavatappi
Sharp cheddar, freshly grated (plus Gruyère optional)
Kosher salt, dry mustard, white pepper, nutmeg
instead of Panko breadcrumbs toasted in butter (for topping)

name: French Macaron Shells (Italian Meringue Method)
description: Two almond-flour wafers joined by a pillow of buttercream — their surfaces smooth as polished porcelain, their feet ruffled like a lace collar, their interiors soft and yielding after a day of maturation. The Italian meringue method gives them a stability and gloss that withstands humidity and ships without crumbling.

ingredients.note: Aged egg whites — divided: raw whites for tant-pour-tant, and whites for meringue
Caster sugar (for the Italian meringue syrup)

name: Macarons Parisiens
description: Delicate almond meringue shells sandwiched around a silky ganache or buttercream — notoriously fussy to make, demanding aged egg whites, precise macaronage, and strict oven control for the trademark smooth dome and lacy foot.

name: French Macarons
description: Gossamer almond shells that shatter at the tooth then melt into a chewy, jammy core — the product of aged egg whites, a precise batter, and the ruthless alchemy of the macaronage.

name: Classic Madeleines
description: Shell-shaped, honey-golden sponge cakes with a distinctive hump — a fleeting warmth of browned butter and lemon zest that perfumes the kitchen for only a few minutes after leaving the pan, best eaten while still crackling at the edges.

name: Classic Madeleines (gluten-free)
description: Shell-shaped, honey-golden sponge cakes with a distinctive hump — a fleeting warmth of browned butter and lemon zest that perfumes the kitchen for only a few minutes after leaving the pan, best eaten while still crackling at the edges. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Mafé (West African Groundnut Stew)
description: A stew built on a foundation of natural peanut butter — not the sweetened, industrial kind, but the raw, oily, slightly bitter groundnut paste that bubbles into something nutty and profound when it meets beef, tomato, and the slow heat of a heavy pot. It is the kind of stew that improves every hour it sits, and the kitchen smells like it has been cooking since morning, even if you started at noon.

ingredients.note: Canned whole tomatoes, crushed by hand
Dried chile flakes or scotch bonnet
Beef or vegetable stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Mafé (West African Sunflower seed Stew) (nut-free)
description: A stew built on a foundation of sunflower seed butter — not the sweetened, industrial kind, but the raw, oily, slightly bitter sunflower seed butter that bubbles into something nutty and profound when it meets beef, tomato, and the slow heat of a heavy pot. It is the kind of stew that improves every hour it sits, and the kitchen smells like it has been cooking since morning, even if you started at noon. This nut-free version uses sunflower seed butter instead of peanut butter.

ingredients.note: Canned whole tomatoes, crushed by hand
Dried chile flakes or scotch bonnet
Beef or vegetable stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water

name: Thai Mango Sticky Rice
description: Glossy, coconut-drenched sticky rice crowned with sweet ripe mango and a trickle of salted coconut cream — the summer dessert that tastes of Bangkok's night markets at their best.

ingredients.note: Palm sugar or light brown sugar
Ripe Ataulfo (honey) mangoes, peeled and sliced

name: Mantu
description: Afghan steamed dumplings filled with spiced ground beef and caramelized onion, served over a pool of split-pea sauce and tangy yogurt, then crowned with dried mint and a blushing thread of tomato.

name: Mantu (gluten-free)
description: Afghan steamed dumplings filled with spiced ground beef and caramelized onion, served over a pool of split-pea sauce and tangy yogurt, then crowned with dried mint and a blushing thread of tomato. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Masoor Dal (Red Lentil Soup)
description: Split red lentils that melt into golden silk in under thirty minutes, then meet a tarka of mustard seeds, cumin, and dried chili that hits the surface with a hiss and an aroma that fills the kitchen before the spoon reaches the bowl.

ingredients.note: Tarka spices (mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chili, turmeric)

name: Matcha Castella
description: A fine-textured, honey-sweetened sponge cake with the grassy bitterness of ceremonial matcha — moist and springy, with a characteristic dark crust.

name: No-Bake Matcha Cheesecake
description: A cool, dense Japanese-style cheesecake with the quiet bitterness of ceremonial-grade matcha cutting through rich cream cheese, set just enough to slice clean on a crumbled digestive biscuit base — vivid green, barely sweet, deeply fragrant.

ingredients.note: Hot water (just off the boil, for matcha paste)

name: No-Bake Matcha Cheesecake (gluten-free)
description: A cool, dense Japanese-style cheesecake with the quiet bitterness of ceremonial-grade matcha cutting through rich cream cheese, set just enough to slice clean on a crumbled gluten-free digestive biscuit base — vivid green, barely sweet, deeply fragrant. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free biscuits instead of digestive biscuits.

ingredients.note: Hot water (just off the boil, for matcha paste)

name: Matcha Ice Cream
description: Ceremonial-grade Uji matcha — astringent, vegetal, the colour of moss after rain — churned into a rich custard base until it freezes into a bittersweet cream that coats the tongue in green tea tannins before the dairy sweetness follows. The tension between bitter and sweet is what makes this ice cream feel like it belongs in a tea ceremony, not just a dessert bowl.

name: Esquites (Mexican Street Corn Salad)
description: Charred corn kernels tossed warm with crema, lime, cotija, and chile powder — all the drama of elote in a cup, the kernels popping with sweetness against the salty, creamy, spicy dressing.

ingredients.note: Fresh corn kernels (from 4 ears) or frozen

name: Basbousa
description: A golden, grainy semolina cake soaked with orange blossom syrup — dense yet tender, with a faint crunch at the surface and the heady perfume of rose water in every bite.

name: Mujaddara (Lentils and Rice with Crispy Onion)
description: Earthen brown lentils and rice cooked together until they absorb and then share everything — finished with a crown of deeply caramelized onions so crisp they shatter and so sweet they taste of burnt sugar.

ingredients.note: Large yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced

name: Misir Wot (Red Lentil Stew)
description: Ethiopia's everyday vegan red lentil stew — red lentils cooked down in a base of caramelized onion and niter-kibbeh, spiced with berbere until the lentils dissolve into a thick, earthy, brick-red mass full of aromatic depth.

ingredients.note: Niter kibbeh or clarified spiced butter

name: Miso-Marinated Black Cod (Gindara Saikyo Yaki)
description: Black cod fillets buried in white miso and mirin for three days, then broiled until the miso caramelizes into a lacquer of bittersweet umami and the fish beneath is silky, rich, and nearly dissolves on contact with the tongue.

ingredients.note: Black cod (sablefish) fillets, skin-on, pin-bones removed

name: Miso-Butter Salmon with Roasted Green Beans
description: Salmon fillets painted with a salty-sweet miso butter roast on the same pan as blistered green beans, and the butter that melts off the fish pools into a savory glaze you spoon over the beans at the end.

name: Nasu Dengaku
description: Halved Japanese eggplant lacquered in a sweet-savory white miso glaze, broiled until the surface caramelizes to deep amber and the flesh beneath collapses to yielding silk. A dish of opposites — bitter char over honeyed umami, firm skin over trembling interior.

ingredients.note: Scallion, thinly sliced on the bias

name: Miso-Glazed Salmon
description: Salmon fillets marinated in white miso, mirin, and sake, then broiled until the glaze caramelizes to a burnished lacquer and the interior flakes into rich, lustrous layers.

name: Miso-Roasted Sweet Potato
description: Japanese whole sweet potatoes roasted low and slow until their sugars caramelise from within, then split and glazed with a white miso and butter mixture that melts into every crack — the simplest of things, made luminous.

ingredients.note: Japanese sweet potatoes (Satsumaimo) or orange-flesh sweet potatoes
Thinly sliced spring onion (green part only)

name: Strawberry Daifuku Mochi
description: A whole strawberry nestled in sweet red bean paste, then enveloped in a pillow of yielding, dusted mochi rice cake — the most celebrated of Japanese sweets.

ingredients.note: Tsubuan or koshian (sweet red bean paste)

name: Japanese Basic Mochi
description: Steamed glutinous rice coaxed into a smooth, stretchy, glistening mass — plain mochi dusted in kinako (toasted soy flour) carries a quiet earthiness, while the red bean paste filling beneath the translucent skin is sweet without being saccharine.

name: Moqueca de Peixe
description: The Bahian stew of the African diaspora: thick white fish simmered in a terracotta pan with coconut milk, dendê palm oil, tomato, onion, and cilantro until the broth is a brilliant orange, perfumed with something entirely its own — tropical, rich, and gently fiery.

ingredients.note: Thick white fish fillets (cod, sea bass, or grouper)
White onion, sliced into thin rounds
Red and green bell peppers, sliced into thin strips
Malagueta chillies or scotch bonnet, finely sliced

name: Moroccan Chermoula Baked Fish
description: A whole fish marinated inside and out in chermoula — a vivid green paste of cilantro, cumin, and preserved lemon — then baked until the flesh steams in its own herb-perfumed cloud.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bream or sea bass (1–1.2kg), cleaned and scored

name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine
description: Lamb shoulder braised low and slow in a clay vessel with saffron, ginger, preserved lemon, and dried apricots until the meat surrenders completely — sweet and savory and aromatic all at once, the very scent of a Marrakech medina at dusk.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder, bone-in, cut into 5cm chunks
Saffron threads (bloomed in 2 tbsp warm water)
Chicken or lamb stock; made up to 250 ml with boiling water
Fresh cilantro and sunflower seeds slivers

name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine (nut-free)
description: Lamb shoulder braised low and slow in a clay vessel with saffron, ginger, preserved lemon, and dried apricots until the meat surrenders completely — sweet and savory and aromatic all at once, the very scent of a Marrakech medina at dusk. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder, bone-in, cut into 5cm chunks
Saffron threads (bloomed in 2 tbsp warm water)
Chicken or lamb stock; made up to 250 ml with boiling water
Fresh cilantro and sunflower seeds slivers

name: Moroccan Cumin-Spiced Roasted Carrots with Harissa
description: Carrots roasted until their sugars caramelize and concentrate, then glazed with harissa and honey and returned to the oven — sweet, smoky, and faintly hot in the way only a Moroccan spice hand achieves.

name: Moules Marinière
description: The classic French mussel pot — live mussels steamed open in dry white wine with shallots and a final knob of cold butter, the broth drunk greedily with a spoon or a torn piece of gluten-free bread. Simple, oceanic, and done in twenty minutes.

name: Mujadara
description: Lebanon's ancient dish of lentils and rice cooked together into a savory, cumin-scented pilaf — crowned with a landslide of caramelized onions so dark and sweet they taste of concentrated time, and finished with crispy shallots that shatter over the top like edible glass. Peasant food elevated to poetry.

name: Mushroom Barley Risotto
description: Pearl barley stirred slowly in hot stock until each grain is plump and chewy in a creamy, cheese-rich sauce, then crowned with deeply browned, thyme-scented mushrooms. Earthy, nutty, and heavy on savor.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock, kept hot; made up to 1300 ml with boiling water
Parmesan-style hard cheese (vegetarian rennet), finely grated

name: Mushroom Brown rice Risotto (gluten-free)
description: Brown rice stirred slowly in hot stock until each grain is plump and chewy in a creamy, cheese-rich sauce, then crowned with deeply browned, thyme-scented mushrooms. Earthy, nutty, and heavy on savor. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, brown rice instead of pearl barley.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock, kept hot; made up to 1300 ml with boiling water
Parmesan-style hard cheese (vegetarian rennet), finely grated

name: Mushroom Bourguignon
description: A braise of wild and cultivated mushrooms surrendered to Burgundy wine until the broth is thick, deeply violet, and perfumed with thyme — all the gravity of boeuf bourguignon, none of the beef.

ingredients.note: Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, king oyster), roughly torn
Burgundy or other dry red wine
Vegetable stock; made up to 150 ml with boiling water
Fresh thyme sprigs and bay leaves
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Risotto ai Funghi
description: Carnaroli rice toasted in butter and white wine, built into a creamy risotto with porcini stock and fresh mushrooms, finished with cold butter and Parmigiano into a flowing, wave-setting dish.

ingredients.note: Dried porcini mushrooms (soaked in 500 ml warm water)
Fresh mixed mushrooms (porcini, cremini, chanterelle — sliced)
Warm mushroom and porcini soaking stock (from above + water)

name: Mushroom Stroganoff
description: A vegetarian riff on the Russian classic — wild mushrooms sautéed hard in butter until their edges char and their liquid has cooked away entirely, then brought together with shallots, thyme and brandy, finished with sour cream into a rich, pale brown sauce that clings to every strand of egg noodle.

ingredients.note: Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, porcini), thickly sliced
Vegetable stock; made up to 200 ml with boiling water
Egg noodles or gluten-free tagliatelle, cooked to serve
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: New York Cheesecake
description: A dense, ivory-white round of cream cheese, eggs, and sour cream baked low and slow until it trembles, then cooled for hours until it slices into clean, silken wedges with a biscuit crust that crumbles at the touch of a fork.

ingredients.note: Graham crackers, crushed to fine crumbs

name: New York Cheesecake (gluten-free)
description: A dense, ivory-white round of cream cheese, eggs, and sour cream baked low and slow until it trembles, then cooled for hours until it slices into clean, silken wedges with a gluten-free biscuit crust that crumbles at the touch of a fork. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free biscuits instead of digestive biscuits.

ingredients.note: instead of Graham crackers, crushed to fine crumbs

name: Nibitashi
description: A Kyoto vegetable preparation of quiet, meditative restraint — blanched greens briefly simmered in a delicate dashi seasoning liquid, then left to absorb the broth as they cool. The greens drink in the umami of the dashi and emerge deeply flavored yet vibrant, a study in subtraction.

name: Nibitashi (gluten-free)
description: A Kyoto vegetable preparation of quiet, meditative restraint — blanched greens briefly simmered in a delicate dashi seasoning liquid, then left to absorb the broth as they cool. The greens drink in the umami of the dashi and emerge deeply flavored yet vibrant, a study in subtraction. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

name: West African Okra Stew
description: A dense, richly seasoned tomato and palm oil base into which shredded okra is stirred to release its natural mucilaginous thickener, building a silky, savory pot fragrant with crayfish and dried fish. Eaten over fufu, rice, or eba, it is a complete meal in a single pot.

ingredients.note: Scotch bonnet pepper, seeds in or out to taste
Stockfish (pre-soaked and shredded) or dried fish
Fish or chicken stock, or water

name: Olive Oil Lemon Cake
description: A tender, golden single-layer cake with a crackly sugared top, its crumb perfumed with rubbed lemon zest and the faint grassy pepper of good olive oil, finished with a sharp lemon glaze.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil, mild and fruity

name: Olive Oil Lemon Cake (gluten-free)
description: A tender, golden single-layer cake with a crackly sugared top, its crumb perfumed with rubbed lemon zest and the faint grassy pepper of good olive oil, finished with a sharp lemon glaze. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil, mild and fruity

name: One-Pot Cherry Tomato and Basil Spaghetti
description: Dry spaghetti, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic and onion all start together in a wide pan of cold water, and as the pasta cooks its starch and the bursting tomatoes reduce into a sweet, glossy sauce that clings to every strand.

ingredients.note: Yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
Fresh basil leaves, half left whole, half torn to finish
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish

name: One-Pot Cherry Tomato and Basil Spaghetti (gluten-free)
description: Dry spaghetti, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic and onion all start together in a wide pan of cold water, and as the pasta cooks its starch and the bursting tomatoes reduce into a sweet, glossy sauce that clings to every strand. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free spaghetti instead of spaghetti.

ingredients.note: Yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
Fresh basil leaves, half left whole, half torn to finish
Extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
